# Tests, CI, bindings and verification index {#sec-ch10}

This chapter documents how pyharp is verified and what a user can rely on. @sec-ch10-test-suite lists the tests
that exist, those the build registers and those the continuous-integration job runs, with the result of running
all of them. @sec-ch10-packaging states which pydisort versions pyharp accepts and what happens when the version it
was built against differs from the one it runs with. @sec-ch10-bindings compares the C++ options with the Python
bindings and the type stubs. @sec-ch10-index indexes the executable checks of this report. Appendix C
(@sec-appc) lists the registered `ctest` tests at the pin.

## Test suite and continuous integration (`ctest`, `pytest`, the `build-and-test` CI job) {#sec-ch10-test-suite}

### Summary

pyharp's tests are of two kinds: C++ programs built with GoogleTest and run by `ctest`, and Python files run by
`pytest`. A reader who wants to know what is verified needs three lists: the tests that exist in the tree, the tests
the build registers, and the tests the continuous-integration job runs. This section gives the three lists at the
pin, the result of running every test that exists, and what that shows about coverage.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** What pyharp's test files check, and which of them CI runs (Tests layer).

**Data.** 22 C++ test files, 7 Python files in `tests/`, 15 in `tests/spectra/`.

**Placement.** `ctest` after a CMake build with `BUILD_TESTS=ON`; `pytest` from the source root.

**Activation.** CMake option `BUILD_TESTS` (default on); CI on every push to `main` and every change proposed against it.

**Guarantee / limits.** CI runs 14 C++ test programs and 3 Python files; the other 27 files are not run.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of @sec-ch10-test-suite.
:::

Local symbols: none.

The C++ tests are registered one by one with the CMake macro `setup_test`; a file that is not named there is
neither built nor run. The Python test files are copied into the build tree but never registered with `ctest`.
The CI job builds the tests, runs `ctest`, and runs three files of `tests/spectra/` with `pytest`.

### Derivation

None: this section states facts about the test harness and has no equations.

### Numerical method

The method here is the harness itself. `setup_test` builds `tests/<name>.cpp` into an executable
`<name>.<build type>` linked against the pyharp library and `gtest_main`, and registers it with `add_test`
(`setup_test`, {{< code cmake/macros/macro_setup_test.cmake repo=pyharp >}}). `tests/CMakeLists.txt`
({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt repo=pyharp >}}) calls it for 14 files; it copies every `tests/*.py` into the build
tree with `configure_file`, but its `add_test(... pytest ...)` line is commented out. The workflow
({{< code .github/workflows/ci.yml repo=pyharp >}}) has one test job, `build-and-test`, on `ubuntu-latest` and
`macOS-latest` with Python 3.11, torch 2.10.0 (the CPU wheel on Linux) and `pydisort==1.7.1` installed with
`--no-deps`; it configures with `-DNETCDF=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON`, runs `ctest --output-on-failure`, and runs
`pytest` on `tests/spectra/test_hitemp_lines.py`, `test_line_kernel.py` and `test_hitran_lines.py`. No job builds
with CUDA.

::: {#cell-fig-ch10-test-suite-coverage .cell execution_count=2}

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2}
![Test files at the pin by category: how many exist (light bars), how many ctest registers (hatched), and how many the CI job runs (dark bars). C++ files that ctest registers are run by CI through ctest; Python files are run only if the workflow names them.](10-verification_files/figure-html/fig-ch10-test-suite-coverage-output-1.svg){#fig-ch10-test-suite-coverage fig-alt='Grouped bar chart. C++: 22 files exist, 14 registered, 14 run by CI. Python tests directory: 7 exist, 0 registered, 0 run. Python tests/spectra: 15 exist, 0 registered, 3 run by CI.'}
:::
:::


Many of the C++ tests are parametrised over device and precision by the fixture `DeviceTest`
({{< code tests/device_testing.hpp DeviceTest repo=pyharp >}}): CPU float32, CPU float64, CUDA float32 and CUDA
float64. `DeviceTest::SetUp` ({{< code tests/device_testing.hpp DeviceTest::SetUp repo=pyharp >}}) skips the CUDA
cases when `torch::cuda::is_available()` is false. The skip tests the torch installation, not whether pyharp was
built with CUDA, so a CPU-only pyharp linked against a CUDA-enabled torch on a machine with a GPU runs the CUDA
cases and fails them (Tests layer below).

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| test registration | {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt repo=pyharp >}} | `setup_test(...)` lines | `BUILD_TESTS` |
| build and register one test | {{< code cmake/macros/macro_setup_test.cmake repo=pyharp >}} | `setup_test` | always |
| device/precision fixture | {{< code tests/device_testing.hpp DeviceTest repo=pyharp >}} | `DeviceTest` | always |
| CUDA skip rule | {{< code tests/device_testing.hpp DeviceTest::SetUp repo=pyharp >}} | `DeviceTest::SetUp` | torch CUDA |
| CI job | {{< code .github/workflows/ci.yml repo=pyharp >}} | `build-and-test` | changes to `main` |

: Code map of the test harness. {#tbl-ch10-test-suite-code}

1. CMake configures with `BUILD_TESTS=ON` (the default) and adds `tests/` ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt repo=pyharp >}}).
2. Each `setup_test(<name>)` builds and registers `<name>.release` in a Release build
   ({{< code cmake/macros/macro_setup_test.cmake repo=pyharp >}}); `setup_test(test_yaml_input)` is
   commented out.
3. The workflow ({{< code .github/workflows/ci.yml repo=pyharp >}}) installs the package and runs `ctest` and the
   three `pytest` files; a failure in any step fails the job.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_inventory.py` `[I1]`-`[I3]` | which files exist, are registered, are run by CI | exact | file listing |
| `run_suite.sh` `[S1]`, `[S2]` | `ctest` with GPUs visible and hidden | pass count | `ctest` |
| `run_suite.sh` `[S3]` | the 8 unregistered C++ files, built out of tree | builds, exit | compiler, gtest |
| `run_suite.sh` `[S4]`, `[S5]` | every Python test file | pass count | `pytest` |

: Checks of the test suite. {#tbl-ch10-test-suite-tests}

The inventory: 22 C++ test files, of which `ctest` registers 14; 3 of the 22 contain no assertion macro
(`test_composition.cpp`, `test_hypsometric.cpp`, `test_yaml_input.cpp`), and `test_bbflux.cpp` asserts only
output shapes. None of the 7 files in `tests/` and 3 of the 15 in `tests/spectra/` are run by CI[^ch10-inv].

Running everything on two source builds of the pin (one against pydisort 1.7.1, one against 1.8.13), on CPU:

- `ctest` passes 14 of 14 with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=` set, as on CI's CPU-only runners; with the GPUs visible it
  passes 11 of 14, because the CUDA cases of `test_toon.release`, `test_water_liquid_mie.release` and
  `test_water_cloud_temperature.release` raise "missing kernel for cuda" on a pyharp built without CUDA[^ch10-run].
- Of the 8 unregistered C++ files, 5 do not compile (`application/application.hpp` is not in the tree), 1 does not
  compile against the current API (`test_yaml_input.cpp`), 1 builds and fails all 3 of its tests (its input
  `example_infrared.yaml` is not in the tree), and 1 builds and exits 0 with no assertion
  (`test_composition.cpp`)[^ch10-run].
- The 7 top-level Python files: 13 tests pass and 1 fails, `test_sonora2020.py`, whose data file must be fetched
  first[^ch10-run].
- The 15 spectra files from the source root: 11 files pass; 8 tests fail in 4 files that CI does not run
  (`test_atm_overview_cli.py` 3, `test_cli.py` 2, `test_output_names.py` 2, `test_molecule_plot_cli.py` 1)[^ch10-run].
  One test of CI's three files, `test_hitemp_lines.py::test_prepare_reads_zip_and_bz2_and_reuses_cache`, asserts
  that a rewritten file gets a new modification time; the suite deselects it and `flaky_rerun.sh` runs it 25 times
  in each environment, with 0 failures in the committed 50 runs[^ch10-flaky].

Apart from the abort of @sec-ch10-packaging, the results are the same for both builds and for the two mixed
pairings.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A green CI run covers the 14 registered C++ programs and 3 spectra files only; the Python tests of the solvers,
including `tests/test_toon.py`, are not run.
:::

- **CI coverage (CANDIDATE, test registration).** 27 of the 44 test files are not run by CI: 8 C++ files are not
  registered and 19 Python files are not named in the workflow[^ch10-inv]. 7 of the 8 unregistered C++ files do
  not build or do not pass, and 8 tests in 4 unrun spectra files fail[^ch10-run].
- **Device gate (CANDIDATE, test fixture).** The CUDA cases run whenever torch reports a GPU, whether or not pyharp
  has CUDA kernels; 3 of 14 `ctest` programs then fail on a CPU-only build[^ch10-run].
- **Assertion-free tests.** `test_hypsometric.release` is registered and asserts nothing; `test_bbflux.release`
  asserts shapes only; the gtest `DeviceTest.simple_toon_mckay89` of `tests/test_toon.cpp` has no assertion.
- **Timestamp-dependent test.** `test_hitemp_lines.py::test_prepare_reads_zip_and_bz2_and_reuses_cache` depends
  on the file system giving two writes different modification times, so it can fail on a coarse clock; it did not
  fail in the committed 50 reruns[^ch10-flaky].
- **Untested combinations.** No CUDA build was available; GPU coverage: answered at @sec-ch09.


## The pydisort dependency and binary compatibility (`pydisort>=1.7.1`) {#sec-ch10-packaging}

### Summary

pyharp compiles against the C++ headers and shared library of an installed pydisort, and at run time loads
whichever pydisort is installed. This section states which versions the package accepts, which one CI tests, and
what happens when the version pyharp was built against differs from the one it runs with.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The pydisort versions pyharp builds and runs against, and the result of mixing them.

**Data.** `pydisort>=1.7.1` (build and run requirement); CI installs 1.7.1.

**Placement.** Build time (CMake finds pydisort) and import time (the extension loads its library).

**Activation.** Always; no option.

**Guarantee / limits.** Matched builds pass; built against 1.7.1 and run with 1.8.13 aborts (Limits layer).

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of @sec-ch10-packaging.
:::

Local symbols: none.

The requirement has a lower bound and no upper bound, so `pip install pyharp` installs the newest pydisort, 1.8.13 when
the checks ran[^ch10-pkg-header], while CI builds and tests against 1.7.1 only.

### Derivation

None: this section states facts about packaging and has no equations.

### Numerical method

At build time `FindDisort.cmake` asks the Python interpreter for the installed `pydisort` package and uses its
headers and `libdisort_release.so` (`__disort_determine_version`,
{{< code cmake/modules/FindDisort.cmake repo=pyharp >}}). The extension built by
`setup.py` (`ext_module`, {{< code setup.py ext_module repo=pyharp >}}) records the run-time search path
`$ORIGIN/../pydisort/lib`, so at import it loads the library of whatever pydisort is installed then. Both
`pyproject.toml` lists, `[build-system] requires` and `[project] dependencies`, say `pydisort>=1.7.1`
({{< code pyproject.toml repo=pyharp >}}); the CI job installs `pydisort==1.7.1` with `--no-deps`
({{< code .github/workflows/ci.yml repo=pyharp >}}).

pyharp's DISORT band solver holds a `DisortImpl` object, a C++ class that pydisort declares in its header
(`DisortImpl`, {{< code src/disort.hpp DisortImpl repo=pydisort >}}). pyharp's compiled code fixes the size and
member layout of that class from the header it was built with, and pydisort's library code uses the layout of its
own header. The two agree only when the versions agree. In the 1.8.13 wheel the header declares one more data
member in `DisortImpl` than at the pin, a `torch::Tensor cuda_workspace_` described as reused CUDA scratch
storage[^ch10-pkg-header].

::: {#cell-fig-ch10-packaging-matrix .cell execution_count=3}

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3}
![Runs of tests/test_rayleigh.py for each pair of the pydisort a pyharp build was compiled against (rows) and the pydisort installed when it runs (columns). Each cell gives the number of clean runs and of runs that ended in a heap-corruption abort; red hatched cells contain aborts.](10-verification_files/figure-html/fig-ch10-packaging-matrix-output-1.svg){#fig-ch10-packaging-matrix fig-alt='A two by two grid. Built 1.7.1 and run 1.7.1: 3 clean. Built 1.8.13 and run 1.8.13: 3 clean. Built 1.8.13 and run 1.7.1: 3 clean. Built 1.7.1 and run 1.8.13: 3 aborted, hatched red.'}
:::
:::


### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| version requirement | {{< code pyproject.toml repo=pyharp >}} | `pydisort>=1.7.1` | always |
| find pydisort at build time | {{< code cmake/modules/FindDisort.cmake repo=pyharp >}} | `__disort_determine_version` | always |
| extension and run-time path | {{< code setup.py ext_module repo=pyharp >}} | `ext_module` | always |
| version CI tests | {{< code .github/workflows/ci.yml repo=pyharp >}} | `pydisort==1.7.1` | CI |
| the shared class | {{< code src/disort.hpp DisortImpl repo=pydisort >}} | `DisortImpl` | DISORT bands |

: Code map of the pydisort dependency. {#tbl-ch10-packaging-code}

1. `pip install pyharp` resolves `pydisort>=1.7.1` to the newest release ({{< code pyproject.toml repo=pyharp >}}).
2. Building from source, CMake reads the version and paths of the installed pydisort
   ({{< code cmake/modules/FindDisort.cmake repo=pyharp >}}) and links its library.
3. Nothing records the pydisort version a build used, and nothing checks it at import.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run_suite.sh` `[S6]` | `tests/test_rayleigh.py` three times per build/run pair | exit 0, no abort | process exit |
| `abi_matrix.py` `[A1]`, `[A2]` | the matrix of @fig-ch10-packaging-matrix | exact counts | `[S6]` lines |

: Checks of the pydisort dependency. {#tbl-ch10-packaging-tests}

No pyharp test runs against more than one pydisort version. The test `tests/test_rayleigh.py` builds a
`RadiationBand` with the DISORT solver, so it constructs and destroys a `DisortImpl`. Each of the four pairings
was run three times: built against 1.7.1 and run with 1.7.1, 3 clean; built against 1.8.13 and run with 1.8.13,
3 clean; built against 1.8.13 and run with 1.7.1, 3 clean; built against 1.7.1 and run with 1.8.13, both tests
pass and then the process aborts with `double free or corruption (!prev)` (exit 134) in 3 of 3
runs[^ch10-pkg-runs]. The rest of the suite gives the same results in all four pairings.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Build pyharp against the pydisort it will run with; a pyharp built against 1.7.1 aborts at exit with 1.8.13.
:::

- **Open bound (CANDIDATE, pydisort compatibility).** `pydisort>=1.7.1` admits 1.8.13, and a pyharp compiled
  against 1.7.1 then corrupts the heap after DISORT runs (3 of 3 runs abort); the matched pairs and the
  1.8.13-built, 1.7.1-run pair do not[^ch10-pkg-runs]. That the cause is the larger `DisortImpl` of 1.8.13
  (the extra member) is a hypothesis consistent with which pair fails; it was not confirmed with a memory checker.
- **Untested combinations.** pydisort releases between 1.7.1 and 1.8.13, and macOS: not provided: no run here
  covered them.

### Summary

pyharp's options are C++ structs; pybind11 code in `python/csrc` exposes them to Python, and hand-written stub
files (`python/*.pyi`) describe them to editors and type checkers. Nothing generates the bindings or the stubs from
the structs, so the three can drift apart. This section compares them option by option at the pin.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Which C++ options a Python user can set, and which the stubs declare.

**Data.** 9 option structs, 58 options and flag accessors; the installed `pyharp` module; `python/*.pyi`.

**Placement.** Import of `pyharp` (bindings); static analysis (stubs).

**Activation.** Always.

**Guarantee / limits.** 16 options have no binding and 29 no stub (Tests layer); none is checked by CI.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of @sec-ch10-bindings.
:::

Local symbols: none.

An option missing from the bindings can be set only through YAML or C++; one missing from the stubs works but is
invisible to type checkers and editor completion.

### Derivation

None: this section compares interfaces and has no equations.

### Numerical method

Each option of a struct is declared with the macro `ADD_ARG(type, name)`, which generates a getter and a setter of
that name; some solver structs add boolean accessors that test a comma-separated `flags` string
(`ToonMcKay89OptionsImpl`, {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89.hpp ToonMcKay89OptionsImpl repo=pyharp >}}). The
bindings expose an option by naming it once more with the macro `ADD_OPTION` of `python/csrc/pyoptions.hpp`, for
example in `bind_rtsolver` ({{< code python/csrc/pyrtsolver.cpp bind_rtsolver repo=pyharp >}}); the stubs declare
it again as a `def` in `python/pyharp.pyi` ({{< code python/pyharp.pyi repo=pyharp >}}). The check
`bindings_diff.py` reads every `ADD_ARG` and flag accessor under `src/`, looks each up as an attribute of the
installed Python class, and as a `def` under the class of the same name in the stubs.

::: {#cell-fig-ch10-bindings-gaps .cell execution_count=4}

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4}

| Toon options | {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89.hpp ToonMcKay89OptionsImpl repo=pyharp >}} | `ToonMcKay89OptionsImpl` | always |

### Summary

Every number this report quotes comes from a committed check. This section is the index of those checks: what each
one checks, how to run it, what it needs, and where its committed output is. It complements Appendix C
(@sec-appc), which lists pyharp's own `ctest` tests at the pin.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** One table of every executable check in the report, with its command and output file.

**Data.** Check scripts and their committed outputs.

**Placement.** Run by hand, by an author before proposing a chapter; not run by the report's CI.

**Activation.** None.

**Guarantee / limits.** Lists the checks present in the report's tree; rows are added as chapters merge.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of @sec-ch10-index.
:::

Local symbols: none.

Checks come in two kinds. Those under `src/pyharp_report/chNN/checks/` verify a chapter's derivations with numpy
or sympy and do not import pyharp. Those under `derivation-checks/chNN/` run pyharp itself, or read the pyharp
tree, and record the build they ran against.

None: this section is an index and has no equations.

- **Coverage of the index.** It lists the checks committed in this tree. Each chapter's checks join it when that
  chapter merges; until then a chapter's own Tests layer is the reference.
